risks: Consolidating 20 pages into others will break existing internal links — need a redirect mapping before any merge
The 6 pages with 0 h2/h3 (inline HTML) need careful restructuring to not break the existing table-of-contents links that are hand-coded in the HTML
Several pages use Hugo shortcodes ({{< faq >}}, {{< product-box >}}) that may not survive restructuring without testing
The 3 draft pages (02, 2026-index, average-by-state) have canonical/redirect already set for 02, but the index page is also draft — need to resolve which is the canonical before merging
Adding sources to 19 zero-source pages is a significant editorial effort — estimated 15-20 hours of research and citation work
unknowns: Whether the site's internal link structure depends on the 20 pages flagged for consolidation (need to check all internal link references before redirecting)
Whether the inline HTML headings in 8 pages are used by the theme's table-of-contents generator (need to check theme templates)
Whether the 3 draft pages were intentionally kept as drafts (they may be placeholders for future work rather than content to remove)
recommendation: Execute the consolidation strategy first: merge the 20 duplicate pages into their targets, set up 301 redirects, and fix all internal links. This eliminates 20.6% of the content base while preserving all value. Then add sources to the 19 zero-source pages (highest priority: the 5 longest pages). Then restructure the 8 pages with inline HTML headings. The 6 replace pages need full rewrites to match their titles. The 41 improve pages need the specific additions prescribed in the table — start with the 15 highest-leverage items.
confidence_basis: Every page was read in full, not sampled. The metrics table was verified against the actual files.
